1. ## **Functional Requirements**

### **1.1.1 Module 1: User and Institution Management**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-M1-01 | The system shall allow new users to register an account using email and password. |
| FR-M1-02 | The system shall send an email verification link to confirm the user's email address. |
| FR-M1-03 | The system shall allow registered deaf travellers to log in to the mobile application. |
| FR-M1-04 | The system shall allow registered institutions to log in to the web-based institutional dashboard. |
| FR-M1-05 | The system shall provide a "Forgot Password" feature to reset passwords via email. |
| FR-M1-06 | The system shall allow users to change their password by providing the old password and a new password. |
| FR-M1-07 | The system shall allow users to log out of the current session. |
| FR-M1-08 | The system shall automatically log out users after 30 minutes of inactivity. |
| FR-M1-09 | The system shall allow users to set their preferred communication method (real-time captioning, text communication, Sign-to-Speech, BIM hand signs, text-to-speech, vibration alerts). |
| FR-M1-10 | The system shall allow users to manage their profile information (name, avatar, age range, nationality, language). |
| FR-M1-11 | The system shall allow users to manage their communication preferences. |
| FR-M1-12 | The system shall allow users to manage their hearing assistance preferences (subtitle font size, display speed, high-contrast mode, full-screen visual alerts, vibration intensity, flash alerts, recognition confidence level). |
| FR-M1-13 | The system shall allow users to manage their emergency contact (add, view, update, delete, set primary). |
| FR-M1-14 | The system shall allow users to set the SOS information receiving order for multiple emergency contacts. |
| FR-M1-15 | The system shall allow users to manage an emergency communication card with hearing impairment note, preferred communication methods, emergency contacts, blood type, allergy information, and important medical notes. |
| FR-M1-16 | The system shall allow airports, hotels, tourist attractions, and transportation facilities to apply for institution registration. |
| FR-M1-17 | The system shall require institutions to provide name, registration documentation, official contact, institution type, and service address during registration. |
| FR-M1-18 | The system shall allow institutions to manage their profile (name, logo, address, contact, operating hours, accessibility service descriptions). |
| FR-M1-19 | The system shall allow institutions to add, view, update, and delete assistance counters. |
| FR-M1-20 | The system shall allow institutions to manage staff in charge. |

### **1.1.2 Module 2: Location-Based Visual Information and Notifications**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-M2-01 | The system shall allow users to identify a participating institution by scanning a QR code, searching, or manually selecting an institution. |
| FR-M2-02 | The system shall support location-based suggestions of nearby participating institutions when location access is enabled. |
| FR-M2-03 | The system shall require the user to confirm the selected institution before starting a venue session. |
| FR-M2-04 | The system shall create and manage a venue session for the selected institution. |
| FR-M2-05 | The system shall display location-specific accessibility information provided by the participating institution. |
| FR-M2-06 | The system shall allow the user to manually end a venue session and automatically end the session when the user leaves the venue. |
| FR-M2-07 | The system shall allow users to activate and deactivate the environment sound alert function. |
| FR-M2-08 | The system shall convert nearby public announcements into real-time text captions using speech recognition. |
| FR-M2-09 | The system shall indicate whether announcement captions originate from official institution data or microphone-based recognition. |
| FR-M2-10 | The system shall detect supported environmental sounds and notify users with visual alerts. |
| FR-M2-11 | The system shall display detected sound information, recognition confidence, and recommended actions where applicable. |
| FR-M2-12 | The system shall receive and display official announcements for users with an active venue session. |
| FR-M2-13 | The system shall prioritise official announcements over microphone-generated captions for the same event. |
| FR-M2-14 | The system shall display announcements according to their priority level (Normal, Important, or Emergency). |
| FR-M2-15 | The system shall notify users of announcements using visual, vibration, or flash notifications based on user preferences. |
| FR-M2-16 | The system shall maintain a history of announcements and notification status. |
| FR-M2-17 | The system shall allow users to register a queue number. |
| FR-M2-18 | The system shall monitor queue progress and notify users when their queue number is approaching or called. |
| FR-M2-19 | The system shall display queue status and related service counter information when available. |
| FR-M2-20 | The system shall notify users when queue information is unavailable or outdated. |
| FR-M2-21 | The system shall provide a notification centre that displays announcements, queue alerts, and environmental sound alerts. |
| FR-M2-22 | The system shall allow users to filter, view, acknowledge, and remove eligible notifications. |
| FR-M2-23 | The system shall allow authorised institution staff to create, edit, publish, schedule, and withdraw visual announcements. |
| FR-M2-24 | The system shall support multilingual announcements and allow authorised staff to review generated translations before publication. |
| FR-M2-25 | The system shall allow authorised institution staff to manage queue information for participating institutions. |
| FR-M2-26 | The system shall deliver queue notifications only to users associated with the relevant queue number. |

### 

### **1.1.3 Module 3:Multimodal Accessible Communication Module**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-M3-01 | The system shall capture live camera video feeds of the user’s hand gestures and body movements.  |
| FR-M3-02 | The system shall translate captured sign language gestures into text strings in real time.  |
| FR-M3-03 | The system shall display a verification screen showing the predicted text alongside an AI confidence score.  |
| FR-M3-04 | The system shall allow the user to manually edit the predicted text on the verification screen.  |
| FR-M3-05 | The system shall allow the user to confirm the predicted text on the verification screen.  |
| FR-M3-06 | The system shall convert confirmed text into spoken audio output via the device speaker.  |
| FR-M3-07 | The system shall map typed text phrases into corresponding sign language video or animation visualizations.  |
| FR-M3-08 | The system shall convert incoming spoken audio from the device microphone into live on-screen text captions.  |
| FR-M3-09 | The system shall convert user-typed text messages into spoken audio output.  |
| FR-M3-10 | The system shall allow the user to adjust the speech playback speed.  |
| FR-M3-11 | The system shall allow the user to adjust the speech playback volume.  |
| FR-M3-12 | The system shall allow the user to select the preferred voice gender for audio synthesis.  |
| FR-M3-13 | The system shall display a split-screen interface to sequence alternating spoken captions and typed text responses.  |
| FR-M3-14 | The system shall translate incoming dialogue text into the user's selected language.  |
| FR-M3-15 | The system shall allow the user to manually correct misidentified text in the dialogue stream.  |
| FR-M3-16 | The system shall allow the user to select predefined context-aware phrases for immediate dialogue insertion.  |
| FR-M3-17 | The system shall save active conversation text logs to local device storage.  |
| FR-M3-18 | The system shall allow the user to clear or delete stored conversation logs.  |

### 

### 

### **1.1.4 Module 4: Sign-Language Reference Engine Module**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| FR-M4-01 | The system shall allow the user to toggle between Malaysian Sign Language (BIM) and American Sign Language (ASL) visual assets.  |
| FR-M4-02 | The system shall display sign language gloss notations (written sign codes) for selected phrases.  |
| FR-M4-03 | The system shall display step-by-step text descriptions of physical hand and body movements alongside the video asset.  |
| FR-M4-04 | The system shall display a library of verified BIM and ASL sign language media organized by travel scenarios.  |
| FR-M4-05 | The system shall allow the user to play sign language video assets.  |
| FR-M4-06 | The system shall allow the user to adjust the video playback speed for sign language assets.  |
| FR-M4-07 | The system shall allow the user to loop sign language video assets continuously.  |
| FR-M4-08 | The system shall allow the user to pause sign language video assets on specific frames.  |
| FR-M4-09 | The system shall allow the user to step forward frame-by-frame through sign language videos.  |
| FR-M4-10 | The system shall allow the user to step backward frame-by-frame through sign language videos.  |
| FR-M4-11 | The system shall allow the user to switch visual perspectives (e.g., front view and side view) for complex sign gestures.  |
| FR-M4-12 | The system shall display sign language video assets in a full-screen display mode for showing to others.  |
| FR-M4-13 | The system shall search for sign language phrases based on text keywords entered by the user.  |
| FR-M4-14 | The system shall filter sign language phrases by specific travel categories (e.g., Airport, Hotel, Restaurant, Emergency).  |
| FR-M4-15 | The system shall display a history list of the user's recent dictionary search queries.  |
| FR-M4-16 | The system shall allow the user to clear their dictionary search history.  |
| FR-M4-17 | The system shall allow the user to bookmark selected sign language phrases into a favorites list.  |
| FR-M4-18 | The system shall display the user's bookmarked favorite phrases on a dedicated quick-access screen.  |
| FR-M4-19 | The system shall allow the user to remove phrases from their favorites list.  |

### 

### **1.1.5 Module 5: Institutional Assistance Request and Response**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| ----- | ----- |
| FR-M5-01 | The system shall allow the user to submit an assistance request by selecting a predefined issue category. |
| FR-M5-02 | The system shall automatically attach the user’s current institution, area, or location to the assistance request if available and permitted by the user. |
| FR-M5-03 | The system shall allow the user to specify their preferred communication method for the assistance request. |
| FR-M5-04 | The system shall allow the user to select the urgency level of the assistance request. |
| FR-M5-05 | The system shall allow the user to upload supporting media or provide a brief text description when submitting an assistance request. |
| FR-M5-06 | The system shall allow the user to track the real-time status of their submitted assistance request. |
| FR-M5-07 | The system shall display incoming assistance requests on the institutional dashboard in real-time. |
| FR-M5-08 | The system shall automatically sort incoming requests on the dashboard based on urgency, waiting time, and user location. |
| FR-M5-09 | The system shall allow institutional staff to accept an incoming assistance request. |
| FR-M5-10 | The system shall allow institutional managers to manually assign an assistance request to a specific staff member. |
| FR-M5-11 | The system shall automatically escalate an assistance request to a supervisor if it remains unaccepted beyond a predefined time threshold. |
| FR-M5-12 | The system shall provide a real-time text communication session between the assigned staff and the user. |
| FR-M5-13 | The system shall allow institutional staff to send predefined quick-reply templates, images, and visual route instructions in the text communication session. |
| FR-M5-14 | The system shall allow the user to reply to institutional staff in the chat using the Sign-to-Text or Sign-to-Speech engine. |
| FR-M5-15 | The system shall allow institutional staff to update the status of the assistance request. |
| FR-M5-16 | The system shall require the user to confirm whether the issue is fully resolved, partially resolved, or unresolved after the staff marks it as resolved. |
| FR-M5-17 | The system shall allow the user to report a non-urgent accessibility issue independently from an immediate assistance request. |
| FR-M5-18 | The system shall record the first response time and total resolution time for each completed assistance request. |
| FR-M5-19 | The system shall allow the user to report specific accessibility issues regarding visual, text, or auditory communication barriers. |
| FR-M5-20 | The system shall allow the user to specify the location of the issue by scanning a QR code, selecting a zone, using GPS location, or entering it manually. |
| FR-M5-21 | The system shall allow the user to categorize the reported issue using predefined tags. |
| FR-M5-22 | The system shall allow the user to select the severity level of the reported issue. |
| FR-M5-23 | The system shall allow the user to input a short text description when reporting an accessibility issue. |
| FR-M5-24 | The system shall allow the user to upload photos as evidence of the accessibility issue. |
| FR-M5-25 | The system shall allow the user to confirm the resolution outcome of their reported issue. |
| FR-M5-26 | The system shall allow the user to provide an accessibility satisfaction rating based on communication ease, response speed, and staff assistance. |
| FR-M5-27 | The system shall require explicit user consent before sharing the reported issue data for institutional aggregated analytics. |
| FR-M5-28 | The system shall allow the user to view their personal history of submitted accessibility issues and their corresponding processing results. |
| FR-M5-29  | The system shall allow the user to cancel an active assistance request before it is resolved by the institutional staff. |

### **1.1.6 Module 6: SOS & Emergency Communication**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| ----- | ----- |
| FR-M6-01 | The system shall allow users to trigger an SOS alert by long-pressing the SOS button. |
| FR-M6-02 | The system shall display a brief countdown (e.g., 3 seconds) after the SOS button is pressed to prevent accidental activation. |
| FR-M6-03 | The system shall allow users to cancel the SOS alert during the countdown period. |
| FR-M6-04 | The system shall proceed with sending the SOS alert if the user does not cancel during the countdown. |
| FR-M6-05 | The system shall send the SOS alert to the user's designated emergency contacts. |
| FR-M6-06 | The system shall send an emergency request to the institution dashboard when the user is located within an affiliated institution. |
| FR-M6-07 | The system shall display the emergency request on the institution dashboard with the user's location and information. |

### **1.1.7 Module 7: Accessibility Analytics Dashboard and Reporting**

| Requirement ID | Functional Requirement |
| ----- | ----- |
| FR-M7-01 | The system shall aggregate and display the total number of confirmed accessibility issues and assistance requests across different institutional areas. |
| FR-M7-02 | The system shall categorize and display issues by predefined types. |
| FR-M7-03 | The system shall allow institutional users to filter accessibility data by time period. |
| FR-M7-04 | The system shall render an interactive heatmap visualizing the physical distribution and frequency of accessibility issues within the venue. |
| FR-M7-05 | The system shall display a ranked list of high-frequency problem locations and common issue categories. |
| FR-M7-06 | The system shall display a low sample size warning and hide percentage calculations if the number of reported issues is too small for statistical significance. |
| FR-M7-07 | The system shall strictly separate standard application feature usage data from confirmed accessibility issue data to prevent false barrier reporting. |
| FR-M7-08 | The system shall calculate and display key service performance indicators including average first response time and average resolution time. |
| FR-M7-09 | The system shall calculate and display the resolution rate, unresolved rate, and repeated request rate for assistance services. |
| FR-M7-10 | The system shall allow institutional managers to compare service performance and user satisfaction scores across different service zones. |
| FR-M7-11 | The system shall allow authorized institutional users to generate automated monthly, area-specific, or problem-category reports. |
| FR-M7-12 | The system shall allow authorized institutional users to export the generated reports and analytics data in supported document and spreadsheet formats. |
| FR-M7-13 | The system shall display issue occurrence trends based on specific times of the day. |
| FR-M7-14 | The system shall display the exact numerical sample size alongside any calculated percentages to ensure data transparency. |
| FR-M7-15 | The system shall calculate and display the total number of assistance requests that exceeded the institution’s predefined response or resolution time limits. |
| FR-M7-16 | The system shall allow institutional managers to view individual staff performance metrics, including the number of requests handled, average response time, and user ratings. |
| FR-M7-17 | The system shall visualize user accessibility satisfaction rating trends over time to track long-term service improvements. |
| FR-M7-18 | The system shall track and display the usage analytics of official visual announcements, including send count, receive count, and user read rates. |

2. ## **Use Case Diagram**

### **1.2.1 Module 1: User and Institution Management**

| Use Case Name: UC-M1-01 \- User Registration |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Wong Yan Thong |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to create a TravelEase account to access the system's features. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M1-01, FR-M1-02 |  |
| **Priority: High** |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. The use case begins when the traveller opens the mobile application and selects "Sign Up". |  |
| **Precondition:**  The TravelEase mobile application is installed and running.  A network connection is required to send the verification email. |  |
| **Postcondition:** A new user account is created and stored in the system.  An email verification link is sent to the user's email address.  The account remains inactive until verified. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user opens the TravelEase mobile application. The user selects "Sign Up". | The system displays the registration form. |
| The user enters email address, password, confirms password, and accepts the terms of service. | The system validates the email format and password strength. \[E1: Invalid Email Format, E2: Weak Password, E3: Password Mismatch\] The system checks if the email is already registered. \[E4: Email Already Registered\] The system creates a new user account with an "inactive" status. The system generates a unique email verification token. The system sends an email verification link to the user's email address. \[A1: Resend Verification Email\] The system displays a success message: "Verification email sent. Please check your inbox." |
| 11\. The user checks their email and clicks the verification link. | 12\. The system validates the verification token. \[E5: Invalid or Expired Token\] 13\.  The system activates the user account. 14\. The system displays a confirmation message: "Email verified successfully. You can now log in." |
| **Alternative Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Resend Verification Email** If the user does not receive the verification email, the user can request to resend. The system generates a new token and resends the verification email. |  |
| **Exceptions:** |  |
| **Invalid Email Format** The system displays an error message: "Please enter a valid email address." The flow returns to step 4\. **Weak Password** The system displays an error message "Password must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character." The flow returns to step 4\. **Password Mismatch** The system displays an error message: "Passwords do not match." The flow returns to step 4\. **Email Already Registered** The system displays an error message "Email already registered. Please login or reset your password." The flow returns to step 4\. **Invalid or Expired Token** The system detects that the verification token is invalid or has expired. The system displays an error message "Verification link is invalid or expired. Please request a new verification email." The flow continues to A1: Resend Verification Email. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC-M1-02 \- Login to Mobile App |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Wong Yan Thong |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a registered deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to log in to the TravelEase mobile application. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M1-03, FR-M1-24 |  |
| **Priority: High** |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. The use case begins when the traveller opens the mobile application and selects "Login". |  |
| **Precondition:**  The TravelEase mobile application is running.  The user has already registered and verified their email.  A network connection is required. |  |
| **Postcondition:**  The user is authenticated and granted access to the TravelEase mobile application. ‘’ A session is created. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user opens the TravelEase mobile application. The user selects "Login". | The system displays the login screen. |
| The user enters email address and password. | The system validates the credentials. \[E1: Invalid Credentials, E2: Account Not Verified, E3: Account Locked\] The system authenticates the user. The system creates a user session. The system records the login timestamp. The system navigates to the application home screen. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events:** |  |
| **A1.      Remember Me** At step 4, the user selects "Remember Me" before logging in. The system stores the session token and automatically logs the user in on subsequent app opens. **A2.      Navigate to Registration** At step 2, the user selects "Don't have an account?" The system navigates to UC-M1-01: User Registration. **A3.      Navigate to Forgot Password** At step 2, the user selects "Forgot Password". The system navigates to UC-M1-03: Forgot Password. |  |
| **Exceptions:** |  |
| **E1.      Invalid Credentials** The system displays an error message "Invalid email or password." The system tracks failed attempts. After 5 failed attempts, the account is locked. The flow returns to step 4\. **E2.      Account Not Verified** The system displays an error message: "Please verify your email before logging in."The flow returns to step 2\.  **E3.      Account Locked** The system displays an error message: "Account locked. Please wait 30 minutes or reset your password." The flow returns to step 2\. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC-M1-03 \- Forgot Password |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Wong Yan Thong |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a user to reset their password if they have forgotten it. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M1-05 |  |
| **Priority: Medium** |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. The use case begins when the user selects "Forgot Password" on the login screen. |  |
| **Precondition:**  The user has already registered.  A network connection is required. |  |
| **Postcondition:**  A password reset link is sent to the user's email. The user can reset their password. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller / Institution Staff |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user selects "Forgot Password" on the login screen. | System display Forgot Password Reset page.  |
| The user enters their registered email address. The user selects the "Send Reset Link" button. | The system validates the email address. \[E1: Email Not Found\] The system generates a unique password reset token. The system sends a password reset link to the user's email address. \[A1: Resend Reset Link\] The system displays a success message: "Password reset link sent. Please check your inbox."  |
| 9\.   The user checks their email and clicks the reset link. | The system validates the reset token. \[E2: Invalid or Expired Token\] The system displays the reset password screen. |
| The system displays the reset password screen. The user selects the "Reset Password" button. | The system validates the password strength. \[E3: Weak Password, E4: Password Mismatch\] The system updates the user's password. The system displays a success message: "Password reset successfully. You can now log in." |
| **Alternative Flow of Events:** |  |
| **A1.      Resend Reset Link** At step 7, if the user does not receive the reset email, the user can select "Resend Reset Link". The system generates a new reset token and resends the password reset link to the user's registered email address. The system displays a message: "New reset link sent. Please check your inbox." The flow returns to step 9\.  |  |
| **Exceptions:** |  |
| **E1.      Email Not Found** The system detects that the email is not registered. The system displays an error message: "No account found with this email." The flow returns to step 4\. **E2.      Invalid or Expired Token** The system detects that the reset token is invalid or has expired. The system displays an error message "Reset link is invalid or expired. Please request a new link." The flow returns to step 3\. **E3.      Weak Password** The system detects that the new password does not meet strength requirements. The system displays an error message: "Password must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character." The flow returns to step 12\. **E4.      Password Mismatch** The system detects that the new password and confirmation do not match. The system displays an error message: "Passwords do not match." The flow returns to step 12\. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC-M1-04 \- Manage Profile |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Wong Yan Thong |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to manage their profile information. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M1-10 |  |
| **Priority: High** |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. The use case begins when the traveller opens the Profile section. |  |
| **Precondition:**  The user is logged in. |  |
| **Postcondition:**  The user's profile information is managed as requested. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user navigates to the Profile section. | The system retrieves the user's profile information. \[E1: No Profile Created\] The system displays the user's profile information (name, avatar, age range, nationality, language). The system displays action buttons which are **Edit Profile and Delete Profile.**  |
| The user selects an action such as Edit Profile, Delete Profile. \[A1:  Edit Profile A2:  Delete Profile\]   | The system saves the updated profile information. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events:** |  |
| **A1.      Edit Profile** At step 5, the user selects Edit Profile. The user updates the desired fields (name, age range, nationality, language). The system validates the inputs. \[E2: Missing Required Fields, E3: Invalid Avatar Format\]. The system saves the updated profile information. The system displays a success message "Profile updated successfully."   **A2.      Delete Profile**  At step 5, the user selects Delete Profile. The system displays a confirmation prompt: "Are you sure you want to delete your profile?". The user confirms deletion. The system deletes the user's profile information. The system displays a success message "Profile deleted successfully."  |  |
| **Exceptions:** |  |
| **E1.      No Profile Created**  At  step 2, if the user has not created a profile yet, the system displays an empty state with a message "No profile found. Please create your profile."  **E2.      Missing Required Fields** During profile creation or update, the system detects missing required fields. The system displays an error message: "Please fill in all required fields." The flow returns to the creation or update form. **E3.      Invalid Avatar Format** The system detects invalid avatar format or size. The system displays an error message: "Please upload a valid image (JPEG, PNG, max 5MB)." The flow returns to the avatar upload step. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC-M1-05 \- Manage Preferences |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Wong Yan Thong |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to manage their communication preferences and hearing assistance preferences. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M1-09, FR-M1-11 |  |
| **Priority: High**  |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. The use case begins when the traveller opens the Preferences section. |  |
| **Precondition:**  The user is logged in. |  |
| **Postcondition:**  The user's communication, language, and hearing assistance preferences are saved as requested. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user navigates to Communication Preferences. | The system retrieves the user's current preferences (communication, language, and hearing assistance). The system displays action buttons: **Edit** and **Reset** to **Default.** |
| The user reviews their current preferences. The user selects an action. | The system processes the selected action. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events:** |  |
| **A1.      Edit Preferences** At step 5, the user selects Edit. The system enables editing mode for all preference sections. The user updates the desired settings (communication methods, languages, hearing assistance settings). The user selects the Save button. The system validates the selections \[E1: Invalid Selection\]. The system saves the user's preferences. The system displays a success message: "Preferences saved successfully." The system refreshes the view page with the updated preferences. **A2.      Reset to Default** At step 5, the user selects Reset to Default. The system displays a confirmation prompt: "Are you sure you want to reset all preferences to default settings?" The user confirms reset. The system resets all preferences (communication, language, and hearing assistance) to default values. The system displays a success message: "Preferences reset to default successfully." The system refreshes the view page with the default preferences. |  |
| **Exceptions:** |  |
| **E1.      Invalid Selection** The system detects an invalid selection (e.g., no communication method selected, duplicate language selection). The system displays an error message: "Please make a valid selection.". |  |

| Use Case Name: UC-M1-06 \- Manage Emergency Contact |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Wong Yan Thong |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to manage their emergency contacts (Add, View, Update, Delete, Set Primary, Set Receiving Order). |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M1-13, FR-M1-14 |  |
| **Priority: High**  |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. The use case begins when the traveller opens the Emergency Contact section. |  |
| **Precondition:**  The user is logged in. |  |
| **Postcondition:**  The user's emergency contacts are managed as requested (added, viewed, updated, deleted, primary set, or receiving order set). |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user navigates to the Emergency Contact section. | The system retrieves the user's emergency contact list. \[E1: No Emergency Contacts Yet\] The system displays the list of emergency contacts with names, relationships, and primary badge (if applicable). ### **1.2.2 Module 2: Location-Based Visual Information and Notifications**

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DewzBZ2huV1DwCZjbb2b2YP7bPr2nVko/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DewzBZ2huV1DwCZjbb2b2YP7bPr2nVko/view?usp=sharing)

| Use Case Name: UC201 \- Start Venue Session |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Liew Jie Er |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow a deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to identify the airport, hotel, tourist attraction, transportation facility or other participating institution that the traveller is currently visiting. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M2-01 to F2-M2-05 |  |
| **Priority:** High |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated.  |  |
| **Precondition:**  TravelEase is running on the user’s device. Camera permission is granted if QR scanning is selected. Location permission is granted if nearby institution suggestions are selected. The selected institution is registered and active. There is no existing venue session. |  |
| **Postcondition:** A venue session is created for the confirmed institution. The venue session start time is recorded. Location-based functions become active. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller, Location Service and QR Code Scanner. |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user opens the institution-identification function. \[A1: Existing Venue Session\] | The system displays the available identification methods: scan QR code, search for institutions and detect nearby institutions. |
| The user selects “Scan QR Code.” \[A1: Search for institutions, A2: Detect nearby institutions\] | The system activates the QR-code scanner. |
| The user positions the QR code provided by the venue within the scanner. | The system reads and validates the QR code. \[E1: Invalid QR code\] The system retrieves the institution information associated with the QR code. The system displays the identified institution name, branch, area and zone type.  |
| The user confirms the institution and area.  | The system creates a venue session. The system displays confirmation that the venue session is active. The system displays information such as accessibility counters. The system enables relevant location-based announcements. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events: Search for institutions** At BF step 3, the user selects “Search Institution.” The system displays a search field and available institution categories. The user enters an institution name or keyword. The system displays matching participating institutions. \[E2: Institution not found\] The user selects an institution. The flow continues from BF step 8\. **Detect nearby institutions** At BF step 3, the user selects “Find Nearby Institution.” The system obtains the approximate device location. \[E3: Location service unavailable\] The system searches for nearby registered institutions. The system displays matching participating institutions. \[E2: Institution not found\] The user selects an institution. The flow continues from BF step 8\. |  |
|  |  |
| **Exceptions: Invalid QR code** The system cannot validate the scanned QR code and rejects the QR code. The system displays an “Invalid QR code” message. **Institution not found** The search result refers to an institution that is unregistered or no longer active. The system displays an “Institution not found” message. **Location service unavailable** The device cannot obtain an approximate location. The system displays an “Location could not be detected” message. |  |
|  |  |
| **Note(s):** Only registered and active institutions may start a venue session. Only one venue session may be active at a time. Nearby institution suggestions depend on location accuracy. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC202 \- End Venue Session |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Liew Jie Er |  |
| **Purpose:** Ends the current venue session manually when the user leaves the institution or automatically when the system detects that the user has moved outside the venue area. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M2-06 |  |
| **Priority:** Medium |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated or system-initiated. |  |
| **Precondition:**  An active venue session exists. |  |
| **Postcondition:** The venue session has ended. The session-end time is recorded. Normal location-based processing is stopped. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller and Location Service. |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user selects “End Venue Session.” \[A1: Automatic session ending\] | The system asks for confirmation. |
| The user confirms that the session should end. | The system records the venue-session end time. The system changes the venue-session status to end. The system stops sending area-specific announcements and queue information associated with the session. The system displays a message that the venue session has ended. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events: Automatic session ending** At BF step 1, the Location Service detects that the user has left the defined venue area. The flow continues from BF step 4\. |  |
|  |  |
| **Exceptions: Location uncertain** The system cannot confirm that the user has left the venue. The system does not automatically end the session. |  |
| **Note(s):** Automatic ending depends on location accuracy and permission. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC203 \- Enable Environment Sound Alert |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Liew Jie Er |  |
| **Purpose:** Allows the user to activate microphone-based captioning for nearby public announcements. TravelEase captures the announcement, converts it into real-time text using speech recognition and sends a visual or push notification when a new caption is available. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M2-07 to FR-M2-11, FR-M2-13 to FR-M2-16 |  |
| **Priority:** High |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated and subsequently event-driven. |  |
| **Precondition:**  The device has a working microphone. Microphone permission is granted. The Speech Recognition Service is available. Announcement caption mode is active. |  |
| **Postcondition:** The caption is displayed and stored in notification history. Caption mode is stopped when deactivated. Raw audio is not permanently stored without permission. |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller, Speech Recognition Service and Push Notification Service. |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user enables the “Environment Sound Alert” function. | The system activates the microphone.  The system starts monitoring environmental audio. The system captures the relevant audio segment and sends it to the Speech Recognition Service. \[E1: Speech recognition service unavailable\] The Speech Recognition Service processes the captured audio. The Speech Recognition Service categorises the sound into 2 types: important sound and public announcement. If a public announcement is detected, the Speech Recognition Service returns the recognised text. \[A1: Important sound detected\] The system displays the recognised announcement as a real-time caption. \[A2: Official announcement is received at the same time, A4: App is running in background\] The system labels the caption as microphone-generated. |
| The user reads the alert or announcement. The user indicates whether the captured announcement was useful. | The system records the usefulness response. |
| The user disables the function | The system stops microphone capture. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events: Important sound detected** If an important sound is detected, the Speech Recognition Service returns the predicted sound and confidence level. The system displays a full-screen visual alert, the sound type, confidence and recommended action. The flow continues from BF step 10\. **Official announcement is received at the same time** The system receives an official institution announcement. The system compares the public-announcement captured with the official institution announcement.  The system displays both announcements in sequence when they appear as different events. \[A3: Official announcement for the same event is received\] The official information is displayed first with an “Official Institution Announcement” label. The microphone-generated caption is displayed after official announcement and remains labelled as automatically transcribed. The flow continues from BF step 10\. **Official announcement for the same event is received** The system prioritises the official announcement when they both appear as the same event and displays only the official announcement with an “Official Institution Announcement” label.  **App is running in background** The Push Notification Service delivers the notification to the user’s device.  The user opens the push notification. The flow continues from BF step 8\. |  |
|  |  |
| **Exceptions: Speech recognition service unavailable** The service is unavailable or connectivity is lost. The system stops live transcription. The system informs the user that caption mode is temporarily unavailable. Official institution announcements remain available when they can still be received. **Speech cannot be recognised** The service cannot convert the public-announcement into readable text. The system displays a transcription-failed message. The system provides a retry option. **Push notification delivery fails** The Push Notification Service cannot deliver the announcement to the user’s device.  The system records the failed delivery and retries according to the configured delivery policy.  The announcement remains available in TravelEase when the application next synchronises with the server. |  |
|  |  |
| **Note(s):** Official announcements take priority. The system must avoid presenting an unsuccessful or very low-confidence transcription as confirmed information.  Speech recognition may be affected by background noise and distance. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC204 \- Receive Official Announcement |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Liew Jie Er |  |
| **Purpose:** Allows a deaf or hard-of-hearing traveller to receive an official visual announcement from a participating airport, hotel, tourist attraction, transportation facility or other institution.  |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M2-09, FR-M2-12 to FR-M2-16 |  |
| **Priority:** High |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** Event-driven and externally initiated. |  |
| **Precondition:**  The user has an active venue session. The institution has published a valid announcement. The announcement has not expired or been withdrawn. |  |
| **Postcondition:** The official announcement is delivered to eligible users when delivery succeeds.  The system records the intended-recipient count, delivery status, opened status and acknowledgement status.  The announcement is stored in the user’s notification history.  |  |
| **Actor:** Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing Traveller, Authorised Institution Staff and Push Notification Service. |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
|  | The institution publishes an official announcement. The system validates the announcement status, target area, and validity period. The system identifies users with matching venue sessions. The system displays the institution name, affected area, priority, time and message. \[A1: App is running in background\] |
| The user reads the announcement. The user marks the announcement as read. | The system records the user’s read status. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events:**  **App is running in background** The Push Notification Service delivers the notification to the user’s device. \[E1: Push notification delivery fails\] The user opens the push notification. The flow continues from BF step 4\. |  |
| **Exceptions: Push notification delivery fails** The Push Notification Service cannot deliver the announcement to the user’s device.  The system records the failed delivery and retries according to the configured delivery policy.  The announcement remains available in TravelEase when the application next synchronises with the server. **Unsupported Alert Method** The device does not support the preferred flash or vibration alert. The system uses available notification methods. |  |
|  |  |
| **Note(s):** Only users with an active venue session may receive area-targeted official announcements.  Official announcements take priority over microphone captions. Push delivery depends on network connectivity. Notification behaviour depends on device capabilities and settings. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC205 \- Track Queue Number |  |
| ----- | ----- |

The system receives subsequent queue updates. The system sends a visual and vibration notification when the number is called. |

| Use Case Name: UC208 \- Manage Institution Queue Information |  |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Author:** Liew Jie Er |  |
| **Purpose:** Allows authorised institution staff to create queue lines and update queue information for a selected queue line, including the current number, upcoming number, counter, service area and queue status. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M2-25 to FR-M2-26 |  |
| **Priority:** Medium |  |

| The staff member selects an existing queue line and enters a new queue number. \[A1: Update current queue number status, A2: Manage queue line, A3: Create new queue line\] | The system validates the information. The system records the queue event. |
| **Alternative Flow of Events: Update current queue number status** The staff member selects called, missed or cancelled for a queue number. The system updates the status. **Manage queue line** The staff member edits the queue line information. The system validates the information. The system records the queue line information. |  |

| **Exceptions: Invalid input** Required content is missing or invalid. The system displays an error message.  |  |

| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The user opens the "Request Assistance" function. | The system displays predefined issue categories, urgency levels, and communication methods. |

| The user taps the "Submit" button. | The system validates the provided inputs.\[E1: Incomplete mandatory fields\] The system creates the assistance request and sets the status to "Pending Acceptance". The system pushes a real-time notification to the Institutional Dashboard. The system displays a real-time status tracker interface to the user. \[A2: Real-time status tracking and cancellation\] |
| **Alternative Flow of Events: A1. Location auto-detection fails** A1.1. At BF step 5, the system cannot automatically pinpoint the user's exact zone. A1.2. At BF step 10, the user stays on the tracking screen and resolves the issue independently before a staff arrives. A2.2. The user clicks "Cancel Request". A2.3. The system prompts for confirmation, updates the request status to "Cancelled", and removes it from the active dashboard queue. |  |
| **Exceptions: E1. Incomplete mandatory fields** E1.1. At BF step 7, the system detects that the issue category or urgency level is missing. E1.2. The system displays an error message highlighting the required fields. E1.3. The flow continues from BF step 3\. |  |
| **Notes:** The system must not allow standard service requests to be tagged as medical emergencies to prevent misuse. |  |

The system routes the request directly to the assigned staff. A1.5. The flow continues from BF step 3\. **A2. Send visual instruction** A2.1. At BF step 5, the staff uploads a map marker or an image instead of text. A2.2. The flow continues from BF step 6\. **A3. Reply using normal text** A3.1. At BF step 7, the traveller types the reply using the device keyboard instead of sign language. A3.2. The flow continues from BF step 8\. |  |

| :---- | :---- |
| **Author:** Jeff Wong Wei Quan |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow institutional managers to view interactive heatmaps of accessibility issues and monitor service performance KPIs concurrently. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M7-01 to FR-M7-10, FR-M7-13 to FR-M7-18 |  |
| **Priority:** High  |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. |  |
| **Precondition:** The Institution Manager is authenticated and authorized to access the dashboard. |  |
| **Postcondition:** The analytical dashboard, heatmaps, and KPI charts are rendered successfully. |  |
| **Actor**: Institution Manager |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The manager navigates to the "Analytics Dashboard" tab. | The system retrieves historical accessibility and performance data. |
| The manager selects a specific time filter (e.g., "This Month"). | The system dynamically and concurrently updates both the interactive heatmap and the Service KPI charts (e.g., Response Time, Resolution Rate). \[E1: No data available\] |
| The manager clicks on a high-frequency zone on the heatmap. | The system displays a breakdown of issue categories, exact sample sizes, and occurrence trends for that zone. \[A1: Low sample size protection\] |
| **Alternative Flow of Events: A1. Low sample size protection** A1.1. At BF step 6, the system detects that the selected zone has too few reported issues for statistical significance. A1.2. The system hides the percentage calculations to prevent data misinterpretation and displays a warning message.  |  |
| **Exceptions: E1. No data available** E1.1. At BF step 4, the system finds zero records matching the time filter. E1.2. The system displays a "No data available for the selected period" message. E1.3. The flow continues from BF step 3\. |  |

| Use Case Name: UC702 \- Generate and Export Report |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Author:** Jeff Wong Wei Quan |  |
| **Purpose:** Allow the manager to compile visual analytics and service KPIs into an automated report and optionally export it to a local file. |  |
| **Requirement Traceability:** FR-M7-11, FR-M7-12 |  |
| **Priority:** Medium |  |
| **Characteristics of activation:** User-initiated. |  |
| **Precondition:** The Institution Manager is authenticated on the dashboard. |  |
| **Postcondition:** A structured report preview is generated and optionally downloaded. |  |
| **Actor**: Institution Manager |  |
| **Main Flow of Events:** |  |
| **Actor Action** | **System Response** |
| The manager navigates to the "Reporting" module. | The system displays report configuration options. |
| The manager sets the date range, selects zones, and clicks "Generate Report". | The system compiles the heatmaps, KPIs, and user satisfaction trends into a formatted document layout. The system displays a preview of the generated report on the screen. |
| The manager clicks the "Export" button and selects "PDF". \[A1: Skip export\] \[A2: Export as CSV/Excel\] | The system applies data anonymization rules to ensure no private traveller identities are exposed. The system converts the report into a PDF file and initiates the download. |
| The manager saves the file. | The system displays a "Download Complete" message. |
